$comment: Superseded by the shared General Provisions blocks in shared.json. Kept for reference: each of these was one document's private copy of a clause that is now written once.

clauses.title: Assignment
clauses.rationale: The change-of-control carve-out is what keeps this clause from blocking the customer's own acquisition; the competitor exception is what a provider asks for in return.
clauses.body: Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the other’s written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, except that either Party may assign it in full to a successor in a merger, reorganization, or sale of substantially all assets. The non-assigning Party may object where the assignee is a direct competitor. Any other purported [[assignment]] is void.

clauses.title: Force Majeure
clauses.rationale: Excusing payment obligations too is the drafting error here. Money is almost never impossible to pay, and a broad clause invites that argument.
clauses.body: Neither Party is liable for a delay or failure caused by an event beyond its reasonable control, including natural disaster, war, terrorism, labor dispute, or failure of a utility or public network. [[Force majeure]] does not excuse a payment obligation. If the event continues beyond {{cure}} days, either Party may terminate the affected Statement of Work on written notice.

clauses.title: Governing Law and Venue
clauses.benchmark: Present in 98% of executed master services agreements
clauses.rationale: The most commonly negotiated general provision, and the one whose absence is most expensive. Naming the home forum of whichever side drafted is the usual starting position.
clauses.body: This Agreement is governed by the laws of {{opStateLong}}, excluding its [[conflict of laws]] rules and the UN Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods. The Parties consent to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the state and federal courts located in {{opStateLong}}.

clauses.title: Notices
clauses.rationale: Several clauses in this agreement run deadlines from a notice, and email-only notice to an individual who has left the company is a common failure.
clauses.body: Notices shall be in writing and sent to the addresses on the signature page, by hand, national overnight courier, or email with confirmation of receipt. Notices of breach, termination, or indemnity claim must also be sent to the recipient’s legal department or general counsel address, where one is stated.

clauses.title: Entire Agreement and Amendment
clauses.rationale: Sales conversations generate expectations that do not appear in the document. This clause decides whether those expectations are part of the deal.
clauses.body: This Agreement, together with each Statement of Work and any addendum, is the entire agreement on its subject matter and supersedes all prior proposals and discussions. It may be amended only by a writing signed by both Parties, subject to <<xr:msa_structure>>.

clauses.title: Governing Law
clauses.rationale: An NDA with no governing law is the cheapest possible way to turn a two-page document into a jurisdictional dispute.
clauses.body: This Agreement is governed by the laws of {{opStateLong}}, without regard to its [[conflict of laws]] principles, and the Parties consent to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts located there.

clauses.title: Amendment
clauses.rationale: An amendment provision that points back to the voting clause keeps the approval thresholds in one place.
clauses.body: This {{govDoc}} may be amended only by a writing signed by the {{ownerTerm}} required to approve amendments under <<xr:@approval>>. No course of dealing or oral statement amends this {{govDoc}}.

clauses.title: Governing Law
clauses.benchmark: Present in 97% of comparable formation packages
clauses.rationale: Without it, which state's law applies is decided by a judge applying conflict-of-laws rules — an expensive way to answer a question you could answer in one sentence.
clauses.body: This [[governing law|governing law]] provision states that this {{govDoc}} shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of {{formStateLong}}, without regard to its [[conflict of laws]] principles. Internal affairs of the Company are governed by {{formStateLong}} law regardless of where the Company operates.

clauses.title: Severability
clauses.rationale: If a court strikes one provision, nothing otherwise tells it to preserve the rest of the document.
clauses.body: If any provision of this {{govDoc}} is held unenforceable, that provision shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it enforceable, and the remaining provisions shall continue in full force. This is a standard [[severability]] provision.

clauses.title: Notices
clauses.rationale: Several clauses in this document run deadlines from a notice. Without delivery mechanics there is no agreed way to prove one was given.
clauses.body: Notices shall be in writing and deemed given when delivered by hand, one business day after deposit with a national overnight courier, or on confirmed transmission by email to the addresses on Schedule A. A party may change its address by notice given under this section.

clauses.title: Entire Agreement
clauses.rationale: Founders accumulate side conversations before formation. This clause decides whether those conversations are part of the deal.
clauses.body: This {{govDoc}}, together with the schedules and exhibits and the other documents in the formation package, is the entire agreement among the parties on its subject matter and supersedes all prior discussions and understandings, whether oral or written.

clauses.title: No Waiver
clauses.rationale: Small companies tolerate breaches informally for years. Without this clause that tolerance can become a waiver of the right itself.
clauses.body: No failure or delay in exercising a right under this {{govDoc}} operates as a waiver of it, and no single or partial exercise precludes any further exercise. A waiver is effective only if in writing and signed by the party granting it.

clauses.title: Termination for Convenience
clauses.rationale: Symmetrical convenience termination protects the provider from being stranded mid-engagement while giving the customer the exit they will ask for anyway.
clauses.body: Either Party may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience on {{renewalNotice}} days’ written notice, whether during the Initial Term or any renewal term. On [[termination for convenience]] the {{counterLabel}} shall pay for Services performed and non-cancellable commitments incurred through the effective date, and the {{selfLabel}} shall refund any prepaid fees for Services not yet performed.

clauses.title: Non-Solicitation of Personnel
clauses.benchmark: Present in 44% of services agreements outside California
clauses.rationale: A buy-out figure is easier to enforce than an outright bar, and it converts a dispute into a number. Void as to California employees regardless of the governing law named.
clauses.body: During the term and for twelve (12) months after, neither Party shall knowingly solicit for employment any individual who performed under this Agreement, except through general advertising or where the individual initiates contact. If a Party hires such an individual, it shall pay a fee equal to fifty percent (50%) of the individual’s first-year base compensation as liquidated damages. This [[non-solicitation]] is not enforceable against individuals working in California.

clauses.title: Dispute Escalation
clauses.benchmark: Present in 57% of master services agreements
clauses.rationale: Most commercial disputes are really unescalated operational disputes. A short executive step resolves a large share of them before counsel is involved.
clauses.body: Before filing suit, the Parties shall escalate any dispute to an executive of each Party with authority to resolve it, who shall confer within fifteen (15) business days. This does not prevent either Party from seeking [[injunctive relief]] under <<xr:nda_injunctive>> at any time.

clauses.title: Non-Solicitation of Personnel
clauses.benchmark: Present in 38% of mutual NDAs outside California
clauses.rationale: Enforceability varies sharply by state, and a general-advertising carve-out is what keeps the clause from being read as a no-hire agreement — which raises antitrust exposure of its own.
clauses.body: For {{termWords}} months, neither Party shall knowingly solicit for employment any employee introduced during the evaluation, except through general advertising not targeted at that person or where the employee initiates contact. This provision is not enforceable against employees working in California.

clauses.title: Dispute Resolution
clauses.benchmark: Present in 71% of comparable formation packages
clauses.rationale: Without a forum clause, any dispute starts with a fight about where to have the fight.
clauses.body: The parties shall attempt in good faith to resolve any dispute through mediation before initiating litigation. Any unresolved dispute shall be brought exclusively in the state or federal courts located in {{formStateLong}}, and each party consents to personal jurisdiction there and waives any objection based on inconvenient forum.

clauses.title: Non-Solicitation
clauses.benchmark: Present in 57% of employment agreements outside California
clauses.rationale: Enforceability turns on duration and scope, and courts in several of these states will narrow rather than strike an overbroad clause — but not all of them will.
clauses.body: For twelve (12) months after employment ends, the {{workerLabel}} shall not solicit any employee of the Company to leave, or solicit any customer they served or learned confidential information about during the final twelve (12) months of employment, for the purpose of providing competing services. This does not restrict general advertising or a customer’s own decision to follow.

clauses.title: Return of Property
clauses.rationale: Withholding a final paycheck until property is returned is unlawful in most states, which is why this obligation has to stand on its own.
clauses.body: On separation or on request, the {{workerLabel}} shall return all Company equipment, credentials, records, and confidential material, and shall permanently delete Company data from personal devices and accounts. The Company may not withhold final wages to enforce this obligation.
